newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed as futures fluctuate.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed as futures fluctuate.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Tuesday as futures markets see-sawed, traders said.
Gasoline eased later as crude gave up early gains. Traders said prices had been held artificially high with crude and the market still looked generally long despite recent run cuts.
Naphtha was also a little weaker with crude but levels were better supported with traders reporting good refiner demand.
"The market is very well supported by demand, particulary in the Med, from refiners for platformer feedstocks," a trader with a U.K. major said, adding that N+A material was still scarce.

Some said that despite good demand outright trade was thin with crude-led volatility keeping buyers and sellers at a standoff and Skikda maintenance limiting avails. However, liquidity is seen improving with Egyptian product available and more Skikda barrels seen emerging around the end of the month.
Gas oil was fairly firm with demand from Turkey, Greece as well as France was supporting the market.
There was some tightness in Russian material with few available cargoes seen coming onto the market in the near term.
One Russian cargo was reported to have traded at roughly quotes cif high +$2.25.
Traders said the cargo offered at quotes cif high +$3.75 on Monday had also been picked up but well below its asking price.
Fuel oil moved with futures but little business was heard done. Demand was seen to cover the latest Portuguese tender.
A little demand was seen for bunker fuel, with one Spanish refiner heard offering at quotes Med fob high +$4-$5. Buying interest was pegged closer to +$2/$2.50.
Low sulphur prices moved with futures, but activity was thin.
